description: Token Generation Predictability If tokens are generated using predictable patterns or weak cryptographic methods, attackers could analyze the token format and generation patterns to predict or generate valid tokens. An attacker captures multiple valid tokens, analyzes their pattern, and creates a script to generate valid tokens, bypassing the queue system.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1528 - Steal Application Access Token
recommendation: Implement secure token generation using cryptographically secure random number generators

description: Queue State Manipulation If access controls to Redis or DynamoDB are not properly configured, or if there are injection vulnerabilities in the queue management logic, an attacker could modify queue state data. An attacker exploits a vulnerability in the queue management API to modify queue positions or counter values, causing legitimate users to experience extremely long wait times.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service
recommendation: Implement strict access controls and validation for queue operations
recommendation: Implement queue state monitoring and anomaly detection

description: Private API Endpoint Exposure Private API endpoints could be exposed through misconfigured network settings, logging of sensitive information, or through DNS enumeration techniques. An attacker discovers private API endpoints through leaked logs or network scanning, then attempts to access administrative functions.
references: recommendation: Implement proper network isolation and access controls
recommendation: Implement comprehensive logging and monitoring

description: Token Storage and Session Management Vulnerabilities Improper token storage, lack of expiration mechanisms, or weak session management could allow tokens to be stolen, reused, or remain valid indefinitely. An attacker captures a valid token and reuses it multiple times to bypass the queue, or uses an expired token that hasn't been properly invalidated.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1539 - Steal Web Session Cookie
recommendation: Implement secure token lifecycle management

description: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) Attack Attackers could send a large volume of requests to overwhelm the system's capacity, particularly targeting the queue management and token generation endpoints. An attacker uses a botnet to generate thousands of queue requests per second, overwhelming the system and preventing legitimate users from accessing the service.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
recommendation: Implement proper monitoring and automated response
